chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Salih ibn Uqbah, from 'Urwah al-Hannat, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who caught a locust and ate it, he said: 'It has blood.' The meaning in this report is that we should interpret it as referring to one who killed many locusts, even if the term 'al-tawhid' (the singular/unique one) was used for it, because he meant the species, and that which indicates this is...

key_terms.التَّوْحِيد: The singular/unique one (referring to a single entity or species)

ai.seo_question: Does a locust have blood according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to resolve the apparent contradiction regarding whether locusts possess blood (dam) by distinguishing between the linguistic generalization of the species and the specific biological reality of large swarms. This reflects the Shia scholarly method of reconciling textual reports through semantic nuance, specifically interpreting 'blood' as a characteristic of the collective mass rather than every individual insect, thereby clarifying dietary laws.
